title: Stability Lens: Weekly Pocket Notes and Handoff Digest
body:
Purpose:
Quick, skimmable notes for the on-call handoff and the weekly SRE sync. This is intentionally terse — keep it in your pocket during the shift.

This week at-a-glance:
- SLO health: overall system availability: 99.90% (7-day window), error-rate SLO breached for request path /v1/generate for ~45m on 2027-07-05.
- Incidents: two notable events (see timeline). Both were mitigated and post-incident tasks are in-flight.
- Handoff flags: one ongoing ops change (kv-cache tuning) requires attention during low-traffic window next Tue.
- Ops focus for next week: reduce tail latency for short-sequence requests, finalize autoscaler cooldown tuning, roll back experimental kernel selection for model-x-small if regressions persist.

Incidents (short form):
1) 2027-07-05 03:18–04:03 UTC — Pairing cascade affecting /v1/generate (P2)
- Summary: A combination of an aggressive model affinity rule and a recent continuous-batching change caused request routing to concentrate on a subset of serving pods. Those pods experienced KV cache pressure and experienced elevated CPU spikes which led to transient queuing and HTTP-5xx responses.
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx rate from 03:15 UTC, error spike in gateway, tail latency climb for short requests.
- Mitigation: temporarily relaxed affinity and manually scaled the affected pool by +20% capacity at 03:31. Fallback routing to a compatible model-variant was enabled at 03:42. Normalized by 04:03.
- Owner: Rajiv (lead on mitigation).
- Follow-ups (ENGOPS-1983): add a routing guard that detects sustained queue growth > 60s and triggers proactive autoscale or temporary affinity softening. Deadline: 2027-07-16.

2) 2027-07-06 18:10–18:29 UTC — S3 ingestion timeout during model artifact fetch (P3)
- Summary: A transient S3 regional throttling event caused a handful of model pulls to stall, increasing cold-start times for some dedicated nodes during rolling updates.
- Symptoms: longer model load times, a small number of client-facing timeouts for scheduled rollouts.
- Mitigation: retried pulls with exponential backoff and switched to cached artifact mirror in us-west at 18:14. Rolling failed updates were aborted and retried after mirror switch.
- Owner: Evelyn.
- Follow-ups: add better artifact mirror failover logic to the deployment controller and add alert for model-pull success rate < 95% over 5m. Deadline: 2027-07-20.

SLO snapshot and anomalies:
- Availability SLO (monthly): target 99.95% — 30d window currently at 99.96% (no concern).
- Error rate SLO (7d for /v1/generate): target 0.5% — observed 0.87% during the window because of the 07-05 incident.
- Latency SLO (p95 short seq): target 200ms — p95 currently at 210ms, p99 at 480ms. Notable tail regressions localized to model-x-small due to current kernel selector experiment.
- Action: schedule a controlled rollback test for kernel-selector on model-x-small in dedicated-canary next Tue evening. Owner: Tomás.

On-call handoff notes (for night shift):
- Active tasks:
  - KV cache tuning rollout (staged) — current canary at 25% traffic. Watch cache miss rate and eviction rate (Grafana panels: kv-cache-evict, kv-cache-miss). Contact: Rajiv.
  - Autoscaler cooldown change in staging — don't promote without passing chaos test. Contact: Leah.
- Alerts to silence/patch: temporary suppression in place for infra-flaky S3 errors (silenced until 2027-07-09 00:00 UTC).
- Escalations: Pager path unchanged; for repeated degraded SLOs escalate to eng-leads channel.

Meeting notes (SRE sync 2027-07-07):
Attendees: Leah, Rajiv, Evelyn, Tomás, Priya K., guest: Kate (infra).
Key discussion:
- Routing guard spec: Rajiv presented draft logic (queue depth + per-pod CPU + KV eviction rate -> trigger). Consensus: ship minimal guard with metric thresholds and safe rollback.
- Autoscaler tuning: Priya highlighted problem of cooldown too short for bursty sequences. Agreed to increase minimum cooldown from 30s to 90s in staging and observe.
- Observability gaps: need a per-variant request fingerprint to tie regressions to kernel-selector choices. Task assigned to Tomás.
Decisions:
- Prioritize routing guard and artifact mirror failover this sprint.
- Defer kernel-selector full rollout until after rollback test.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Rajiv: routing guard initial PR + unit tests (due 2027-07-13).
- Evelyn: deployment-controller mirror failover RFC + small POC (due 2027-07-14).
- Tomás: per-variant fingerprint instrumentation + Grafana panels (due 2027-07-12).
- Leah: coordinate canary rollback plan and ops runbook entry for kernel-selector (due 2027-07-11).

Runbook / quick check for oncall (one-pager):
1) If you see /v1/generate errors > 0.8% sustained for 5m -> check routing heatmap and per-pod queue length. If more than 30% of requests target <20% of pods, relax affinity (temporary) and trigger autoscale.
2) If model pulls start timing out -> switch to artifact mirror, abort rolling updates, notify infra on Slack and open short incident channel.
3) Tail latency spike for short requests -> check kernel-selector experiment flag for the variant; rollback to baseline if p99 > 600ms for >10m.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider a lightweight synthetic workload that exercises short-sequence requests across all pools every 3m — would detect routing concentration faster.
- Explore adding a KV-cache eviction metric into the routing decision loop (long-term).

Appendix (links):
- Incident ticket ENGOPS-1983 (routing cascade)
- Deployment controller PR draft (github.com/redwood-inference/deploy/pull/452)
- SLO dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/slo-dashboard
- On-call rotation: Confluence page CFT-ops/oncall-rotation

End of pocket notes. Keep this doc as the canonical short-handoff for the week. Update status to in_review once follow-ups are PRs in review.
